quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ken Sharp on Wraith Shield and radios: Wraith Shield (a software upload that networks smart radios to detect and jam drones, with no change to the radio or antenna) was built with L3Harris's own investment under commercial item determination, without an RFP; it is 'still in development', there is no first sale yet, L3Harris is 'working with SOCOM on it', and it will be integrated, with the radios, into the VAMPIRE system. Falcon IV (domestic) and Falcon III (international) refreshes come shortly; a fifth-tier supplier slowdown is causing some bumps, but L3Harris expects good growth exiting the year and into next year; it received its first NGC2 order ('our fair share') and the HMS and Marine Corps budget lines are up. The CSD margin guide stays at mid-20s to keep funding R&D.

CFO Ken Sharp on space and ISR: L3Harris was 'the only prime that actually launched a satellite, and it actually worked' and 'the only prime to win all five' missile-warning / missile-tracking tranches, with about 70 satellites in the process of being built; it made a $93 million investment in AMDT3 ahead of the award to be ahead on schedule. Space programs are booked at margins 'far below what we're bidding at' ('If you bid at 15%, we're booking at 10%', earning the higher rate through execution). The maritime part of ISR has been slower and is expected to accelerate; ISR aircraft revenue is lumpy and margin-dilutive because L3Harris buys the aircraft itself.
quarterly_data.figure: about 70 satellites in build; $93 million invested in AMDT3 ahead of award

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ken Sharp on missiles and the portfolio: L3Harris 'sold 60% of the commercial space propulsion' business; it has invested over $2 billion in missile capacitization ahead of contract ('we spent $2.2 billion ahead of contract to go put shovels in the ground, invest in the supply chain'). He says there are 'two of them really of scale in the U.S.' in solid-fuel rocket motors, and L3Harris has a seeker 'ready to go tomorrow' that it thinks is more manufacturable if the missile architecture opens up.
quarterly_data.figure: 60% of commercial space propulsion sold; $2.2 billion invested ahead of contract
